text: Thanks for joining. The goal today is to lock the scope of the customer data export so Leo can size it.
For Compliance, "customer data" has to include derived and analytics data, not just the profile fields.
From the Product side I've been scoping "customer data" as profile data only, so the export stays small.
Privacy Policy v3 is explicit on this. It says customer data covers all data we hold about a customer, including derived analytics.

The estimate swings a lot. Profile data only is about one sprint. Adding derived and analytics data is closer to four, because those tables live in the warehouse and have no per-customer export path today.
The roadmap says this ships this sprint. Could we do profile data first and add the rest later?
A partial export can be fine as a first release, but we can't call it complete, and it can't be how we answer a data subject request.
Then I don't want to commit to a number until the two of you agree on one definition. I'll size both scopes and post them in the channel.
Okay. We hold the estimate, Leo sizes both scopes, and Sana and I come back with one definition.
Today is about whether automated identity checks are ready for the pilot. Rafael, do you want to start with the Risk view?
Our tolerance for false positives is two percent. Above that, too many legitimate customers land in manual review and we can't clear the queue.
Two percent is also what the Risk Policy says since September. At that level we can hold our 24 hour review commitment.
Hold on, we built to five percent. That's the number in the vendor integration spec, version one.
That spec is from the spring. The policy moved to two percent after that.
Nobody told us. The threshold is a config value, but reaching two percent means the vendor retrains the match model, and that's about two weeks plus a new test run.
Then the pilot waits. I can't sign off on five percent.
Separate concern. The integration keeps ID document images for 24 months. Our retention standard says 90 days for government ID images.
We use those images to review appeals and tune the fraud rules. Ninety days is shorter than most of our appeal cases.
Then we need an exception on record, or a way to keep what you need without the raw image. Right now there's no approved retention period.
So two outcomes. The pilot is on hold until Eng retunes to two percent, and Amir and Dana bring back a retention proposal.
We need a call on MFA for enterprise SSO before Nina's team starts the sprint.
Security's position is that MFA is required for every account that signs in to an enterprise workspace, admins especially.
If we force MFA on day one we hurt trials. Growth needs signup to stay frictionless, with a new user in the product in under a minute.
We've seen MFA at first login cost around thirty percent of trial signups.
Where is that number from?
It's from memory, an older funnel analysis. I don't have the dashboard handy.
Eng can do either. Prompting later is a small change as long as we decide before the sprint starts.
I can live with optional MFA during a trial if we revisit it after the pen test.
Then for now MFA is optional during trials, and we revisit it after the pen test.
The pen test results are in, so we're back on last week's MFA decision.
The testers got into a trial workspace with a reused password and invited themselves as admin. Trial workspaces connected to SSO hold real customer directory data.
That's the scenario I was worried about. Optional MFA has to go for any workspace connected to SSO, trials included.
Trial conversion is still my number. Can we at least not ask on the very first screen?
We can. Require MFA when someone turns on the SSO connection, not at signup. Email-only trial signups stay as they are.
That closes the finding, as long as no SSO connection can exist without MFA.
I can accept that. I still want to watch the funnel for a few weeks.
Decision: MFA is required before any workspace enables SSO, trials included. This replaces last week's decision.
